player_safe.name: Zephra Exchange
player_safe.public_face: A market and toll-house brand that promises orderly crossing, registered cargo, and trade access.
player_safe.slogan: Zephra™: the price of everything, the value of you.
player_safe.short_description: Zephra Exchange™ runs the market, the toll, and the stamp that decides whether your movement counts as legal.
player_safe.long_description: The Zephra™ tollhouse is bureaucratic theater: brass scales, a queue rope, a clerk stamping Movement Legitimacy™ certificates under a banner reading FREE TRADE in expensive gold leaf. Register your cargo, buy a Crossing Credit™, upgrade to a Priority Passage™ pass that lets you skip the line you are also paying to maintain. Prices float by the hour on a big chalk board nobody can quite read. They did not build the river or the road. They built the gate, the fee, and the cheerful word for the fee, which is 'civilization,' and they will sell you a pamphlet explaining why the toll is freedom.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The Zephra stamp lands with a delicate click. The clerk does not raise their voice. They do not need to. The road, apparently, has standards.

block1.name: Zephra Exchange
block1.public_face: A market and toll-house brand that promises orderly crossing, registered cargo, and trade access.
block1.what_they_really_do: Gatekeeps access and engineers scarcity while teaching people to call the fee civilization.
block1.place_in_story: Zephra route optimization helped cut Bramble workers loose and makes checkpoint delays feel official.

block1.the_lever: Evidence, embarrassment, liability, or a public contradiction moves them more than moral appeal.

block2.standing: The territory's clearinghouse for trade and movement, the brand that decides whose crossing is legitimate this season.
block2.what_they_control: A market and toll-house brand that promises orderly crossing, registered cargo, and trade access.
block2.how_they_operate: Gatekeep access and manufacture scarcity: own the chokepoints, float the prices, and rebrand the fee as order so nobody calls it a wall.
block2.internal_tensions: True believers and tired workers keep the public promise alive while managers monetize the gap between promise and harm.
block2.current_moves: Repricing old routes and issuing stamps that decide whose movement counts as legitimate.
block2.history_hook: Institutional beliefs: Access Fee Purge; Commodity Sentiment Engineering; Guild Courtesy as Class Weapon.

block3.who_they_prey_on: Traders, migrants, and anyone whose right to move can be made conditional on a stamp Zephra alone can sell.

block4.slogan: Zephra™: the price of everything, the value of you.

voice: FREE trade! (Stamping, registration, and crossing fees apply.)
Today's crossing rate is... let me check the board. It went up.
You're not paying a toll. You're investing in order!

player_safe.name: Goldspire Logistics
player_safe.public_face: A forgettable freight-coordination concern with plain grey seals and paperwork nobody remembers seeing twice.
player_safe.short_description: A dull freight mark, a grey seal, and a name too boring to remember keep Goldspire Logistics nearly invisible.
player_safe.long_description: Goldspire Logistics does not look powerful. That is the trick of it. A grey seal appears on crate corners, approval slips, and route papers, always in the same modest ink, always small enough to miss if you are looking for a villain with a banner.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The mark is almost nothing: grey ink, a square crate, a practical little stamp in the corner. It has the confidence of something that does not need to advertise.

block1.name: Goldspire Logistics

block1.what_they_really_do: GM-only: coordinates the staged competition, manages scarcity, and turns danger and protection into the same product line.
block1.place_in_story: Never on stage. It is the unseen pressure behind contracts, routes, prices, and impossible paperwork.
block1.disposition_to_pcs: Does not know the PCs exist yet, which is part of the horror.
block1.the_lever: No lever in this one-shot. The party can only begin to glimpse a pattern.

block2.standing: Total and invisible, like a stage manager for a play the audience thinks is real.
block2.what_they_control: Brands, prices, road dangers, protection products, custody paperwork, and the illusion of choice.

block2.internal_tensions: The owned brands jockey for favor; that friction is a future crack, not a one-shot reveal.
block2.current_moves: Rebalancing which roads are dangerous this season to keep protection demand healthy.
block2.history_hook: The moment competing concerns quietly merged behind a bland name and discovered coordinated scarcity outperformed real competition.

block3.who_they_prey_on: Everyone, framed as serving everyone.

voice: It never speaks directly. It speaks through everyone else's slogans.
block4.logo_hook: A plain freight-crate sigil that hides every other mark in miniature.
block4.theme_song_hook: Silence, or polite office music nobody admits hearing. Seed only.

block5.hidden_ties: GM-only deepest layer: every corporate faction routes upward into this bland center.

official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

outcomes.hard_failure: A flat read of Emeris Capital Gate hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: None.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

rolls.fear_spin: GM gains Fear. Add pressure, reveal cost, spotlight a threat, or advance a visible consequence.

player_safe.name: Emeris Capital Gate
player_safe.short: A great arch of pale carved stone three wagons wide, with toll-counters clacking beneath it and the green dark of Sablewood waiting beyond.
player_safe.one_line: A great arch of pale carved stone three wagons wide, with toll-counters clacking beneath it and the green dark of Sablewood waiting beyond.
player_safe.read_aloud: A great arch of pale carved stone rises three wagons wide, its keystone leafed in gold and its faces worn smooth by a century of carved caravans setting out. Beneath it runs a permanent little fair: toll-counters clacking, a crier calling the morning rates, a stall hawking painted gate-charms, and the smell of fried dough and hot sealing-wax.
player_safe.long_body:
The Emeris Capital Gate is the city showing off the threshold of the wild. Pale carved stone rises three wagons wide, its keystone leafed in gold, its surfaces worn smooth by a century of carved caravans setting out. Carts queue in the cool of the arch's shadow, and past it the paved road runs straight into the green dark of Sablewood.

Beneath the arch lives a permanent little fair. Toll-counters clack. A crier calls the morning rates. A stall sells painted gate-charms to travelers who already bought three other kinds of courage. The air smells of fried dough, hot sealing-wax, horse-goat harness, and forest rain waiting just beyond the wall.

There is no ward missing here and nothing broken in the public face of the gate. The drama is simpler and more useful: this is where city confidence becomes road risk.
player_safe.known_for: The western threshold of Emeris, route tolls, courier departures, gate charms, caravan queues, and the first straight look into Sablewood.
player_safe.culture_food: Travelers buy fried dough, hot spiced cider, route tokens, painted gate charms, and advice from people who may or may not have survived the road themselves.
player_safe.travel_texture: Passing under the gate cools the air for one breath. Then the city noise falls behind and the forest sound comes forward.

Emeris.name: Emeris
Emeris.summary: A walled city of honey-colored stone on the very lip of the great forest, where the last paved road in the world meets the first wild tree.
Emeris.role: Emeris is the dispatch point, territory capital, and Sablewood-edge start city. It is safe and prosperous at the start; keep active ward crisis language in Hush scenes.

player_safe.name: Emeris
player_safe.short: A walled city of honey-colored stone on the very lip of the great forest, where the last paved road in the world meets the first wild tree.
player_safe.one_line: A walled city of honey-colored stone on the very lip of the great forest, where the last paved road in the world meets the first wild tree.
player_safe.read_aloud: Emeris is a prosperous walled city built where the paved world ends and Sablewood begins. Honey-colored houses climb gentle streets toward a great western gate, banners hang from crowded windows, and the air smells of fresh bread, ink, oiled leather, and the green breath of the forest.
player_safe.long_body:
Emeris is the capital of its own territory and proud of it, a tight, prosperous walled city built where the paved world ends and Sablewood begins. Its houses are honey-colored stone with steep painted shingles, crowded shoulder to shoulder up gentle streets that all seem to bend, eventually, toward the great gate in the western wall. Banners hang from every other window, half of them advertising something.

The markets are loud and good-natured. This is a courier town as much as a capital, so the talk is all of routes and weather and who got back from the forest and who did not. Caravans are loaded in the squares at dawn, and licensed guides hawk their route knowledge like fruit. The smell is fresh bread, ink, oiled leather, and the green breath of the forest leaking over the wall.

The people are frontier-prosperous: friendly, busy, a little boastful, with the particular confidence of folk who have never once doubted that their city is safe. They will tell you Emeris is the finest city in the territory, and within the territory they are not wrong.
player_safe.known_for: The last paved, walled comfort before Sablewood, courier and caravan trade, its great Capital Gate, painted shingles, route gossip, and festivals.
player_safe.culture_food: Emeris treats routes as gossip and safe returns as public celebration. Street food is fried festival dough, skewered river fish, and hot spiced cider sold at the gate to travelers heading into the trees.
player_safe.travel_texture: Leaving Emeris feels like walking out of bread, bells, and stone into green shadow. The road stays paved just long enough to make the first mud feel like a decision.

player_safe.name: Athervast
player_safe.short: A city like a coiled crown, where gold-capped towers rise from the center and the rings spiral outward, lower and louder, until the gleam becomes rumor.
player_safe.one_line: A city like a coiled crown, where gold-capped towers rise from the center and the rings spiral outward, lower and louder, until the gleam becomes rumor.
player_safe.read_aloud: Athervast does not have a skyline so much as a spiral. At its heart stand grand pale towers capped in gold, so tall that clouds catch on them, and from that crown the whole city winds outward in vast circular tiers like the inside of a shell.
player_safe.long_body:
Athervast does not have a skyline so much as a spiral. At its heart stand the grand towers, pale stone capped in gold, so tall that the clouds catch on them, and from that crown the whole city winds outward in vast circular tiers like the inside of a shell, ring within ring within ring. It is the kind of place that makes you think of Atlantis, if Atlantis had been bought and rebranded.

Up in the highest rings the streets are quite literally gold, swept clean every hour, quiet but for the splash of fountains and the soft chime of a thousand floating witch-lights. This is where the elites live and rule. They are carried, not walked. The air up here smells of citrus, cold stone, and money.

Drop a tier or two and the city gets brighter and far louder. The entertainment district never sleeps: enormous magical illusions bloom across the open sky, silent dragons and dancing giants and grinning corporate mascots a hundred feet tall, drifting between towers like colored smoke. Crowds pour out of illusion-theatres and luck-halls, criers sell tickets to wonders that may or may not be real, and the streets taste of spun sugar, spilled wine, and perfume.

Further out, the rings turn to work. Here are the great manufactories: long glass-roofed halls where laborers stir steaming vats of Hexmart healing draughts and bottle them by the thousand, the air gone sharp with mint and copper and something faintly medicinal. The streets here are honest stone, not gold. The people move fast and tired. They make everything the gold rings drink.
player_safe.known_for: Gold streets in the high rings, sky-illusions in the entertainment tiers, potion manufactories in the workrings, and the public claim that it is the safest and grandest city on Terra.
player_safe.culture_food: Status is altitude. Up top: candied citrus and iced wine. In the bright rings: sugar twists, skewers, cheap dazzling cocktails. In the workrings: hard bread and bitter green tonic the factory crews drink to keep their hands steady.
player_safe.travel_texture: Athervast is not on the one-shot route. If it appears, it should feel distant, huge, aspirational, and insulated from the road's mud.

player_safe.name: The Goldspire Relay
player_safe.short: A twisting stone signal-spire of mirrors, flags, and courier-birds, its beacon flickering thinner than it should.
player_safe.one_line: A twisting stone signal-spire of mirrors, flags, and courier-birds, its beacon flickering thinner than it should.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Goldspire Relay twists upward like maintenance became monument, its weak fire making future failure visible.
player_safe.long_body:
Wind, beacon-light, signal-workers, ridge paths, anxious maintenance, and a view wide enough to imply the rest of the story. The world feels like it is answering back from up here.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Signal yard: Mirrors, flags, and courier birds make communication visible. Beacon chamber: The light source flickers with meaning. Ridge overlook: The view connects every prior place at once. Maintenance stair: Narrow steps and tool niches make the spire feel worked, not decorative.

Plants and materials: wind-bent ridge grass, lichen on signal stones, small herbs in stair cracks. Animals and background life: courier birds, ridge insects, tiny cliff goats that ignore danger. The air carries beacon pulse, high wind, signal chime, far storm light. Messages arrive, are questioned, encoded, relayed, delayed, and sometimes quietly corrected.

What people can get here: message relay, ridge lodging, maintenance supplies.
player_safe.known_for: A stone spire that twists upward as if maintenance kept turning into monument. The signal yard flashes with mirrors, flags, and courier-birds. The beacon chamber flickers with meaning. From the ridge overlook you can see every place you have been at once, and the narrow maintenance stair makes plain this is a worked tower, not a decorative one.
player_safe.culture_food: Signal crews eat in shifts at the yard, one hand always free for a flag, bread and hard cheese and a tea brewed strong enough to survive the wind. The courier-birds get the scraps and the affection both.
player_safe.travel_texture: The beacon pulses, high wind tugs at your cloak, signal-chimes ring out of time with each other. Far storm-light flickers along the horizon. Messages arrive, get questioned, encoded, relayed, and sometimes quietly corrected, and you feel the whole web of the world tugging on this one thin point.

block1.disposition_default: Unseen, urgent, lonely, and fiercely competent.
block1.the_lever: Players who protect messages, maps, and living keepers earn the cleanest future opening.

block2.wants_now: Be heard before the relay failure becomes someone else's ruin.
block2.larger_motivation: Keep a distant signal alive long enough for help to choose the road.
block2.wants: Be heard before the relay failure becomes someone else's ruin.
block2.motivation: Keep a distant signal alive long enough for help to choose the road.
block2.personality: Keeps a dying signal alive out of sheer refusal. Wears braids threaded with bells tuned to far spires; two of them no longer ring, and she will not remove them, because silence is still evidence.
voice: The relay does not answer. A cold bell rings once, then stops with the rope still trembling.
block2.secrets: The exact cause of the failing relay remains future-story material.
block2.fears: A bell ringing with no one left to answer it.

likes_dislikes.likes: Clear signals, maintained lenses, and messages answered before they become prayers.
likes_dislikes.dislikes: Silence treated as consent and distant trouble treated as tomorrow's paperwork.

block2.likes: Clear signals, maintained lenses, and messages answered before they become prayers.
block2.dislikes: Silence treated as consent and distant trouble treated as tomorrow's paperwork.
block2.favorite_thing: A cracked signal lens that still catches one clean star.
block2.loved_ones: Other keepers in the relay chain, including the Whitefire Custodian's worried memory of them.
block2.day_to_day: Listens to bells, trims wick-lights, polishes lenses, and marks missed pulses on a cord.
block2.appearance: An older woman in dark teal maintenance robes stands in a stone relay chamber, silver-black braids threaded with tiny copper bells, blue crystal earrings, a cracked glowing lens in one hand and a charred map ribbon in the other. Full-body reference: Full-body older relay keeper in dark teal medieval maintenance robes, layered key belts, stamped seal tags, charm chains, practical boots, cracked blue relay lens, charred map ribbon, and hanging brass bells, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Service-poor, tool-rich; everything valuable is attached to the relay's survival.
block2.animal_companion: No animal; fireflies gather near the lens when the signal weakens.
block2.physical: An older woman in dark teal maintenance robes stands in a stone relay chamber, silver-black braids threaded with tiny copper bells, blue crystal earrings, a cracked glowing lens in one hand and a charred map ribbon in the other.

block2.body_language: Leans as though hearing a far bell no one else can.
block2.quirks: Reads torn maps by touch before trusting what the ink says.

player_safe.name: Underroot
player_safe.short: A concealed web of tunnels and homes carved among roots where off-ledger communities survive below the dangerous surface.
player_safe.one_line: A concealed web of tunnels and homes carved among roots where off-ledger communities survive below the dangerous surface.
player_safe.read_aloud: Underroot is not a dungeon; it is a concealed neighborhood of root rooms, low lanterns, and people who survive below the route economy.
player_safe.long_body:
Underroot is the forest's underside: damp passages, glowing fungus, root doors, old animal routes, and the sense that the ground has a memory.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Root tunnel: Twisting roots make walls, ceiling, and handholds. Glowfungus chamber: Soft light turns water drops and old stones into landmarks. Flood pocket: A low chamber holds dark water and hidden movement.

Plants and materials: glowfungus shelves, pale root hairs, water moss, small blind flowers. Animals and background life: Centi-Beetles carve low tunnels, Spidermanders press ash-damp feet into soft walls, Hellbender legends make every tremor feel observed, Fox-Bats sleep in warm cracks. The air carries drips echoing too far, earth-warm air, root doors creaking as they grow, fungus light dimming near noise. Roots pull water down, fungus turns rot into light, insects feed on fungus, and larger animals use the tunnels during storms.
player_safe.known_for: This is not a dungeon, it is somewhere people live, down where the official map stops. Roots make the walls and the ceiling and the handholds. Soft fungus-light turns water drops and old stones into landmarks. Low doorways open on rooms warmed by the earth itself, and the air tastes of damp and lamp-smoke.
player_safe.culture_food: Food comes up from below and out of the dark, pale fungus, blind fish, roots boiled soft, a thin sweet beer brewed in a hollow. It is shared carefully, because everything down here was hard to get, and a guest who wastes it is not a guest for long.
player_safe.travel_texture: You duck and the world goes close and warm. Drips echo too far in the dark. Root-doors creak as they keep growing, and the fungus-light dims when you raise your voice, as if the place itself is asking you to keep it down.

block2.known_for: This is not a dungeon, it is somewhere people live, down where the official map stops. Roots make the walls and the ceiling and the handholds. Soft fungus-light turns water drops and old stones into landmarks. Low doorways open on rooms warmed by the earth itself, and the air tastes of damp and lamp-smoke.
block2.culture_food: Food comes up from below and out of the dark, pale fungus, blind fish, roots boiled soft, a thin sweet beer brewed in a hollow. It is shared carefully, because everything down here was hard to get, and a guest who wastes it is not a guest for long.
block2.travel_texture: You duck and the world goes close and warm. Drips echo too far in the dark. Root-doors creak as they keep growing, and the fungus-light dims when you raise your voice, as if the place itself is asking you to keep it down.

player_safe.name: The Titan's Steps
player_safe.short: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.
player_safe.one_line: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Titan's Steps climb through height, rope, sweat, and hazard pay until travel itself feels like a negotiated risk.
player_safe.long_body:
Each stair is a plaza. Each crack is a path. Every climb is a small expedition, and the people who run it have learned to laugh at the size of the place so it does not crush them.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Lower grass step: Grass and flowers turn a single stair into a meadow. Crack path: A split in the stone is wide enough to walk through. Overlook lip: The edge gives a dizzying view across the territory.

Plants and materials: wind grass, step flowers, crack-root shrubs, lichen maps. Animals and background life: ridge goats, stone swifts, crack crickets, little lizards basking on warm stone. The air carries wind rise, warm stone, huge shadows, distant echo. Rain fills cracks, flowers bloom in steps, goats graze the platforms, and old carved channels guide water down.

What people can get here: wind shelter, rare herbs, high vantage.
player_safe.known_for: Each stair is the size of a town square, so a single step takes half a morning to climb. Grass and flowers have turned the lower treads into hanging meadows. A crack in the stone becomes a road you walk down the middle of. From the lip, the whole territory unrolls so far below that birds pass beneath your boots.
player_safe.culture_food: Climbers eat light and often, hard biscuit, dried meat, a sharp tea brewed at altitude to keep the hands steady. Hazard pay buys better rations near the top, and people guard a warm flask like a secret worth keeping.
player_safe.travel_texture: The wind rises with you and the air thins until your chest works for every breath. Warm stone underfoot, huge cold shadows overhead. An echo you started comes back to you changed, and you feel, in a dizzy funny way, very small and very alive.

player_safe.name: Duskwatch Exchange
player_safe.short: A Sablewood trade point where route knowledge, watches, and liability-backed bargains change hands above or beside the old wood.
player_safe.one_line: A Sablewood trade point where route knowledge, watches, and liability-backed bargains change hands above or beside the old wood.
player_safe.read_aloud: Duskwatch Exchange is where route knowledge changes hands quietly, because the forest charges more for ignorance.
player_safe.long_body:
Duskwatch Exchange is a trade post at the hour when everyone wants business done before dark: lantern counters, route boards, package yards, food smoke, and tired guards.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Lantern counters: Merchants trade goods under warm low light. Watch platform: A raised lookout watches road, sky, and crowd. Package yard: Crates, straps, seals, and arguments make terrain.

Plants and materials: dusty hedge rows, lantern herbs, tough road weeds. Animals and background life: pack beetles, courier birds, dusk moths, tired road ponies. The air carries lantern smoke, bell calls, seal wax smell, twilight chill. Business peaks at dusk, then the exchange becomes watchful, quiet, and protective.

What people can get here: trade goods, package handling, road news, cheap hot food.
player_safe.known_for: Everyone wants their business done before dark, so the whole place moves at a hurried, friendly clip until the light goes. Lantern counters glow under low awnings. A raised platform keeps watch on road and sky at once. The yard fills with crates, straps, wax seals, and the particular arguments of tired people with somewhere to be.
player_safe.culture_food: Hot food comes off a smoking griddle fast and cheap, skewers, fried roots, a strong dark stew ladled to anyone with a coin and a hurry. The cider is warm, and the portions get bigger as the light gets lower.
player_safe.travel_texture: Lantern smoke and seal-wax in the cooling air, bells calling the last trades. As dusk drops the bargaining quiets and the place turns watchful, doors easing shut, lanterns pulled in, the whole exchange listening to the dark beyond the wood.

player_safe.name: The Catcher's Cradles
player_safe.short: A cradle system associated with the Titan's Steps, letting Sablewood's logistics guild make vertical risk look routine.
player_safe.one_line: A cradle system associated with the Titan's Steps, letting Sablewood's logistics guild make vertical risk look routine.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Catcher's Cradles make vertical danger look routine: suspended nets, rescue platforms, and the quiet pride of people who catch mistakes for a living.
player_safe.long_body:
The Catcher's Cradles are practical and absurd: huge nets, hanging baskets, pulley towers, safety flags, caught debris, and workers who judge people by how they handle rope.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Lower net field: Big nets sag under old catches. Pulley posts: Ropes and baskets create vertical movement. Repair platform: Workers patch nets and gossip overhead.

Plants and materials: rope vines, wind moss on poles, snagged seed pods. Animals and background life: nesting swifts, net spiders, beetles eating old rope fibers. The air carries rope twang, net sway, pulley squeal, sudden drops stopped by fabric. The cradles catch falling cargo, branches, animals, and pride; workers sort what can be saved.

What people can get here: rope work, salvage, fall-safe crossing.
player_safe.known_for: Huge nets sag between the trees, heavy with a century of caught things, branches, crates, the occasional boot. Pulley towers haul baskets up and down. Safety flags snap overhead. The workers size up a newcomer entirely by how they handle a rope, and they are usually right.
player_safe.culture_food: The crews eat on the repair platforms, passing a shared pot hand to hand so no one has to climb down for it. Plain food, beans and bread and strong tea, eaten with the easy gallows-humor of people who catch other people's mistakes for a living.
player_safe.travel_texture: Ropes twang and nets sway as you cross. Something drops nearby and is caught with a soft enormous whump you feel in your teeth. The workers move like the height is nothing, and watch to see whether you can do the same.

player_safe.name: The Lucent River
player_safe.short: A luminous river whose blue night glow lets travelers keep time and whose waters are sold, mythologized, healed by, and hunted in.
player_safe.one_line: A luminous river whose blue night glow lets travelers keep time and whose waters are sold, mythologized, healed by, and hunted in.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Lucent River carries blue light through Sablewood like a road that refuses to become a road.
player_safe.long_body:
The Lucent River is beautiful navigation: glowing current, rope ferries, shrine stones, shallow crossings, and water bright enough to make secrets feel visible.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Rope ferry: A small ferry crosses the bright current. Shrine bank: Tiny offerings sit where the river bends. Glow shallows: The riverbed shines through clear water.

Plants and materials: river reeds, glow algae, bank herbs, water lilies with pale undersides. Animals and background life: Craymeleon-pulled boats work the current, Eeligator ripples cut the glowing shallows, glass fish flash under the rope ferry. The air carries blue light from below, rope creak, current whisper, wet stone coolness. Algae bloom with moon and ward pulses; fish follow light, birds follow fish, and ferry workers follow all of it.

What people can get here: ferry crossing, river food, local shrine customs.
player_safe.known_for: The water carries its own blue light, bright enough at night to read by, so the river looks like a road that refused to become one. A small rope ferry hauls across the current. Tiny offerings sit on the bank where the water bends. In the shallows the glowing riverbed shines up through your own reflection.
player_safe.culture_food: Ferry folk grill glass-fish caught straight from the bright water, sweet and faintly luminous, and sell river-cress by the handful. Pilgrims buy little bottles of the glow, which is mostly algae and entirely hope.
player_safe.travel_texture: Blue light rises from below and lights you from the wrong direction, so faces look strange and honest at once. The ferry rope creaks, the current whispers, the wet stones breathe cold, and you catch yourself lowering your voice without meaning to.

player_safe.name: The High Falls
player_safe.short: The place where the Lucent River drops into a cave system that once held a community nobody can fully explain.
player_safe.one_line: The place where the Lucent River drops into a cave system that once held a community nobody can fully explain.
player_safe.read_aloud: The High Falls drown speech in blue-white spray where the Lucent River drops into a cave mouth nobody fully explains.
player_safe.long_body:
The High Falls are loud, wet, and vertical: rainbow mist, rope overlooks, slick ledges, tents near the spray, and conversation that has to become gesture.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Mist overlook: The falls drown out small talk. Spray path: A slick path crosses behind or beside falling water. Lower pool: Cold water gathers with floating flowers and debris.

Plants and materials: spray moss, cliff flowers, water ferns, roots gripping wet stone. Animals and background life: Craymeleon shells flash near mooring ropes, Eeligator shadows move below the lower pool, mist swifts hunt through spray. The air carries roar, rainbow mist, slippery stone, sudden cold gusts. Mist feeds moss, moss holds insects, insects feed birds, and falling water erases tracks unless someone knows where spray cannot reach.

What people can get here: clean water, cold storage, hidden conversation space.
player_safe.known_for: The Lucent River throws itself off a cliff into a cave mouth no one has fully mapped, and the roar swallows every word. Blue-white spray hangs in a permanent rainbow. Slick ledges thread behind the falling water. Tents cluster just out of the spray, and the people in them do not raise their voices because they cannot.
player_safe.culture_food: Cold is the whole pantry here. The spray keeps fish and milk and cut fruit fresh on the lower ledges, and travelers trade for the luxury of something genuinely chilled. A kettle has to be carried well back from the water just to be heard to boil.
player_safe.travel_texture: The roar arrives before the falls do and takes your words with it. Spray beads on everything, the stone goes treacherous underfoot, and cold gusts shove up out of the pool. Conversation becomes hands and eyebrows, and the falling water quietly erases your tracks behind you.

player_safe.name: The Miremist
player_safe.short: A mist-wrapped place where route certainty breaks down and the forest makes navigation feel like an audit of attention.
player_safe.one_line: A mist-wrapped place where route certainty breaks down and the forest makes navigation feel like an audit of attention.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Miremist makes certainty expensive: fog, wet roots, and route sounds that arrive from the wrong distance.
player_safe.long_body:
The Miremist feels like a place with opinions about navigation: luminous puddles, crooked posts, soft ground, cheerful warning charms, and paths that are only paths at the right time.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Post trail: Crooked markers cross wet ground. Soft pool: Still water hides depth and reflection tricks. Dry hummock: Small islands hold plants, nests, and temporary safety.

Plants and materials: bog moss, pitcher flowers, reed mats, floating lantern algae. Animals and background life: Mist-Things move as half-seen animal shapes, Eeligator wakes disturb deep pools, Ward-Moths drift where old lines run under water. The air carries low mist, sucking mud, reflected lights, muffled sound. Mist rises as water warms, insects gather at lights, frogs follow insects, and the safe path changes with water level.

What people can get here: rare herbs, hidden paths, quiet hiding places.
player_safe.known_for: The fog has opinions about where you are going. Crooked posts mark a trail that is only a trail at the right water level. Luminous puddles double the lights and lie about distance. Cheerful little warning-charms dangle from the posts, and the soft ground makes no promises about holding your weight.
player_safe.culture_food: Almost nothing safe to eat grows out here, but the mire hides rare herbs worth a fortune to anyone brave or foolish enough to fetch them. Foragers carry their own bread and trust nothing they did not pack themselves.
player_safe.travel_texture: Sound arrives from the wrong distance, a voice close that should be far, a bird far that should be close. Mud sucks at every step. Reflected lights drift where there is no lamp, and certainty becomes the most expensive thing you are carrying.

player_safe.name: The Stones of the Vale
player_safe.short: Tall carved stones with mossy grooves and offerings that are always fresh, where the light lingers a half-second too long in the gaps between them.
player_safe.one_line: Tall carved stones with mossy grooves and offerings that are always fresh, where the light lingers a half-second too long in the gaps between them.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Stones of the Vale glow blue at the edges, as if old protection is waking up angry and tired.
player_safe.long_body:
The Stones of the Vale are quiet and old: carved grooves, offerings, flowered grass, light between stones, and a sense of being measured by something patient.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Outer stones: Tall stones frame the approach. Offering hollow: Small gifts reveal local relationship to the place. Light gap: A gap between stones catches light unnaturally.

Plants and materials: stone flowers, groove moss, short sweet grass, tiny rootlets in carvings. Animals and background life: crickets, small birds, patient pollinators, lizards warming on stone. The air carries stone warmth, quiet wind, light alignment, low ward resonance. The stones gather dew, feed moss, shelter insects, and mark seasonal light paths people still half-remember.

What people can get here: quiet counsel, seasonal markers, ritual context.
player_safe.known_for: Tall carved stones frame the approach, their grooves worn soft and packed with moss. Small offerings sit in a hollow between them, fresh, which means someone still comes. Light catches wrong in the gap between two of the stones and lingers a half-second too long. You get the distinct sense of being measured by something patient.
player_safe.culture_food: No one trades here. People leave food rather than eat it, a heel of bread, a comb of honey, a cup of something poured straight onto the ground for whatever is listening.
player_safe.travel_texture: The stones hold the day's warmth long after the air has gone cool. The wind drops to almost nothing between them. A low resonance sits under everything, more felt than heard, and you find yourself stepping softly without anyone telling you to.

player_safe.name: The Claravale Market
player_safe.short: A warm market surface where the wonder of Sablewood becomes ordinary food, handmade craft, and gossip before it becomes corporate product.
player_safe.one_line: A warm market surface where the wonder of Sablewood becomes ordinary food, handmade craft, and gossip before it becomes corporate product.
player_safe.read_aloud: Claravale Market turns Sablewood wonder into breakfast, gossip, patched tools, and ordinary bargaining.
player_safe.long_body:
Awnings, food steam, loud bargaining, charm sellers, crafts, spices, strange livestock. People from a dozen districts crowd the same alleys, and every single one of them wants something.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Food spine: Hot food stalls create the market's smell map. Charm row: Real and fake charms compete loudly. Courier corner: Messages, route news, and jobs trade hands. Back awnings: Shadowed tables hold private bargains.

Plants and materials: hanging herbs, fruit pyramids, flower ropes, shade vines over awnings. Animals and background life: pack beetles, bright chickens, tiny drakes, spice moths. The air carries steam, bells, crowd tide, spilled sugar, charm sparks. Morning produce, midday bargaining, afternoon gossip, evening entertainment, and night deals all change the same alleys.

What people can get here: food, charms, tools, route gossip, livestock, repairs, private introductions.
player_safe.known_for: Awnings in every color lean over stalls packed too close together. The smell hits in bands as you walk, smoke, then spice, then sugar, then something alive in a crate. Real charms and fake charms sell side by side at the top of their sellers' voices. In a quiet corner, couriers trade route-news and jobs in a private code of nods.
player_safe.culture_food: This is where Sablewood's wonder becomes breakfast. Skewers char over open coals, fruit stacked in bright pyramids, strange livestock eyeing you from pens, a dozen cooks each certain theirs is the one to try. You eat walking, and your hands are sticky before you have made it down a single row.
player_safe.travel_texture: The crowd takes you like a current. Bells, haggling, the spark and pop of a charm-seller's trick. Spilled sugar underfoot and the warm tide of bodies, and every few steps someone is selling you something you did not know you wanted.

player_safe.name: The Sunless Farms
player_safe.short: A farming region shaped by canopy-darkness, local ingenuity, and crops that do not need corporate sunlight to grow.
player_safe.one_line: A farming region shaped by canopy-darkness, local ingenuity, and crops that do not need corporate sunlight to grow.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Sunless Farms grow under canopy-darkness, proving that lack of official sunlight never meant lack of life.
player_safe.long_body:
The Sunless Farms make farming feel magical and practical at once: shaded crops, fungus lamps, careful schedules, and people who know how to grow food where sunlight barely visits.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Glow-crop beds: Pale crops grow in luminous rows. Fungus lamp racks: Living lights are tended like livestock. Compost heat pits: Warm pits feed the growth cycle.

Plants and materials: pale root vegetables, glowmoss, cap mushrooms, shade beans. Animals and background life: white beetles aerate soil, soft blind mice steal seeds, moth larvae pollinate night flowers. The air carries lamp fungus pulse, warm compost steam, cool overhead darkness. Fungus light feeds crops; crop scraps feed compost; compost warms fungus racks and keeps the farms alive.

What people can get here: shade crops, fungus lamps, quiet worker knowledge.
player_safe.known_for: Crops grow here without the sun ever reaching them, pale rows lit by racks of living fungus-lamps tended like livestock. Compost pits breathe warmth up through the beds. The workers move by a careful schedule of light and heat, and they will tell you, with quiet pride, that they never needed the sun the company kept trying to sell them.
player_safe.culture_food: The harvest is strange and good, pale roots sweet as chestnuts, mushrooms the size of fists, beans grown in the dark that taste faintly of smoke. Workers eat what does not sell, ladled hot from a pot kept warm on a compost vent.
player_safe.travel_texture: You step from forest gloom into a deeper, stranger dark, lit pale green from below. The air is warm and close and smells of rich earth and growing things. Lamps pulse softly as someone tends them, and the cool overhead dark sits over it all like a held breath.

player_safe.name: The Refuge
player_safe.short: A prosperous Sablewood settlement where hazard rate becomes money, reputation, and a quiet measure of who survives the route.
player_safe.one_line: A prosperous Sablewood settlement where hazard rate becomes money, reputation, and a quiet measure of who survives the route.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Refuge is prosperous because people learned how to survive Sablewood, not because Sablewood became safe.
player_safe.long_body:
The Refuge feels warm but not static: soup, blankets, repairs, whispers, small injuries, and people deciding whether rest is enough.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Common room: Chairs, blankets, and bowls make safety visible. Supply corner: Practical goods show what the place can offer. Back exit: A quiet way out keeps safety from becoming a trap.

Plants and materials: potted herbs, dried moss bundles, medicinal roots. Animals and background life: Rabbit-Gliders skim near the fishing lines, Moth-Possums cling in warm rafters, Turtle-Mice work the crumb paths, Badger-Hawks dive for catches outside. The air carries soup steam, low voices, blanket smell, wardstone night-light. People arrive shaken, get fed, exchange news, repair gear, and leave with slightly steadier hands.

What people can get here: rest, food, minor healing supplies, safe rumor exchange.
player_safe.known_for: People arrive here shaken and leave a little steadier. The common room is all chairs and blankets and bowls, safety made visible. A wardstone burns low as a nightlight. There is always a quiet way out the back, because the folk who run this place know that a refuge with only one door is a trap.
player_safe.culture_food: Soup is the whole welcome, thick and hot and pressed on you before you have sat down. The blankets smell of woodsmoke. There is bread, and broth, and the particular kindness of people who were once the ones arriving cold and never forgot it.
player_safe.travel_texture: The door opens on warmth and low voices and the smell of soup, and something in your shoulders comes down an inch. People nurse small injuries, swap road-news in murmurs, and decide, slowly, whether rest is enough or whether they have to move on tonight.

player_safe.one_line: A route or ritualized path where fire becomes both danger and logistics credential in Sablewood's local economy.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Fire Walk smells of ash, resin, and ritualized courage, a path where heat is both danger and credential.
player_safe.long_body:
The Fire Walk is a practical hazard turned local ritual: hot stones, safety ropes, heat vents, sweating travelers, and a weird pride about crossing properly.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Cool staging stones: People gather courage before the heat. Vent path: Heat vents create timing and route pressure. Rest pocket: A safe middle space lets players breathe.

Plants and materials: heat flowers, ash moss, red-edged grasses. Animals and background life: heat lizards, ash beetles, bold little birds that steal cooled crumbs. The air carries heat shimmer, stone tick, sweat, sudden flame blossoms. Heat vents pulse, plants bloom in warm cracks, insects graze ash moss, and locals read the crossing by rhythm.

What people can get here: crossing guidance, heat herbs, local bragging rights.
player_safe.known_for: Heat shimmers off the stones before you reach them. Travelers gather on the cool rocks to work up their nerve, then cross a path where vents breathe fire on their own timing. There is a strange local pride about doing it properly, and an unspoken scorn for anyone who runs.
player_safe.culture_food: They roast on the heat for free, peppers blistered black, flatbread slapped onto hot stone, a fierce little liquor passed around to settle the nerves. Crossing earns you a bitter, smoky tea and the right to brag about it forever.
player_safe.travel_texture: The air bends with heat and the stone ticks as it swells. Sweat starts before you take a step. You time your crossing to the pulse of the vents, flame blooming and dying, and come out the far side scorched, shaking, and quietly thrilled with yourself.

player_safe.name: The Ash Quarry
player_safe.short: A quarry where ash has practical value, letting the setting show resource extraction without losing the strangeness of the old wood.
player_safe.one_line: A quarry where ash has practical value, letting the setting show resource extraction without losing the strangeness of the old wood.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Ash Quarry turns ancient residue into industry: gray terraces, warm dust, and workers who know which piles still remember fire.
player_safe.long_body:
The Ash Quarry feels industrial in a fantasy way: pale dust, ramps, ledges, rope lifts, lunch sheds, stone carts, and workers who know every dangerous shortcut.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Stepped cuts: Stone ledges create height and sightlines. Lift winches: Ropes and platforms move stone and people. Ash pile flats: Soft pale dust records movement.

Plants and materials: ash scrub, hardy grey flowers, dust-coated weeds. Animals and background life: Spidermanders coat themselves in ash, Badger-Hawks raid lunch lines from above, dust mice and quarry swifts scatter when ropes strain. The air carries powdery air, rope strain, stone clack, echoing coughs. Dust coats plants, insects feed on mineral bloom, birds nest in cut ledges, and workers reshape the quarry daily.

What people can get here: stone work, labor gossip, tools, high-low route knowledge.
player_safe.known_for: Pale dust coats everything, the ramps, the ropes, the coughing crews. Stone ledges step down into the cut, and rope-lifts haul slabs and people up and down together. Soft ash flats record every footprint. The workers know which piles still hold heat, which is to say which ones still remember being on fire.
player_safe.culture_food: Lunch is eaten gray-handed in a dusty shed, hard bread, salt pork, a tea that crunches faintly no matter how careful you are. The water is kept covered, and a clean cup is a small daily victory worth defending.
player_safe.travel_texture: The air turns powdery and dries your throat raw. Ropes strain, stone clacks, and coughs echo off the cut walls. Your boots print deep in the soft ash, and a fine pale grit settles into every crease of you before you have done a single thing.

player_safe.name: Root's Hollow
player_safe.short: A settlement whose alchemists brave Sablewood and the Lucent River for healing water, roots, herbs, and careful local knowledge.
player_safe.one_line: A settlement whose alchemists brave Sablewood and the Lucent River for healing water, roots, herbs, and careful local knowledge.
player_safe.read_aloud: Root's Hollow smells of tinctures, river water, and careful survival, a place where alchemists learn from Sablewood because they have to.
player_safe.long_body:
Root's Hollow is small and warm because everything above it is enormous and indifferent. You sit under a ceiling of living roots, lanterns in the niches and boots drying by the door, feeling like you crawled in under the ribs of something vast and asleep.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Central root room: A low fire or lantern marks the shared space. Crawl exits: Small exits lead to several different ground-level places. Storage nook: Practical caches show who uses the hollow.

Plants and materials: root hairs, soft moss beds, tiny fungus lamps. Animals and background life: Spidermanders leave ash-damp prints, Centi-Beetles scrape under the soil, Hellbender stories make the ground feel like it is listening. The air carries earth smell, muffled outside sound, root warmth, lantern smoke. Travelers shelter, animals scavenge, roots grow slowly around forgotten objects.

What people can get here: shelter, hidden cache, quiet exit.
player_safe.known_for: The room sits down inside the roots, low enough that tall folk learn to stoop fast. Lanterns hang in niches worn smooth by hands. Drying herbs and stoppered tinctures crowd every shelf, and the whole place smells of river water and crushed leaves. Boots cake with mud at the door, because everyone here has just been out in the wet for something.
player_safe.culture_food: Food is medicine here and medicine is food, bitter root teas, broths thick with foraged greens, bread you chew slowly because it is mostly seeds. They press a warm cup into your hands the moment you sit, and watch to make sure you finish all of it.
player_safe.travel_texture: You duck under a root and the forest noise drops to a hush, replaced by drip and lantern-smoke and the smell of turned earth. The ceiling breathes down close. Small exits branch off into the dark, each one leading somewhere different, and the warmth comes up out of the ground itself.

player_safe.name: The Latch
player_safe.short: A settlement or gateway whose name makes local access feel earned rather than purchased.
player_safe.one_line: A settlement or gateway whose name makes local access feel earned rather than purchased.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Latch feels like a threshold that decides whether access is earned, bought, or refused.
player_safe.long_body:
The Latch is a crossing with personality: crank wheels, oversized locks, bridge teeth, dangling key charms, and a mechanism that seems offended by haste.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Gate bridge: The crossing narrows where the mechanism grips it. Crank platform: Controls are exposed, heavy, and tempting. Maintenance hatch: A crawl space gives clever players another route.

Plants and materials: lock-moss in gear teeth, bridge weeds, dangling vine knots. Animals and background life: gear beetles, bridge swallows, crank mice. The air carries metal groan, charm clatter, bridge shudder, satisfying or terrifying clicks. The mechanism jams, gets coaxed open, collects moss, and is cleaned just enough to remain stubborn.

What people can get here: controlled crossing, mechanism clues, shortcut if understood.
player_safe.known_for: A crossing that grips the road like a fist. Oversized locks and crank-wheels clamp a bridge that narrows where the mechanism bites it. Key-charms dangle and clatter in the wind. The whole contraption seems personally offended by anyone in a hurry, and lets you across on its own stubborn schedule.
player_safe.culture_food: Whoever tends the Latch keeps a kettle and a grudge, and will share both. There is bread and hard cheese and strong tea for those who wait politely, and a markedly longer wait for those who do not.
player_safe.travel_texture: Metal groans, charms clatter, the bridge shudders under the mechanism's grip. You hear the clicks, satisfying when they go your way and stomach-dropping when they do not, and you learn fast that the Latch decides this, not you.

player_safe.name: The Sable Stills
player_safe.short: A settlement where strong drink, old jokes, and Sablewood craft turn danger into hospitality without making danger harmless.
player_safe.one_line: A settlement where strong drink, old jokes, and Sablewood craft turn danger into hospitality without making danger harmless.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Sable Stills are warm, smoky, and sharper than they seem, turning old wood, strong drink, and local jokes into hospitality with teeth.
player_safe.long_body:
The Sable Stills should smell illegal before it looks illegal: copper coils, moss smoke, bubbling barrels, hidden paths, and workers insisting this is all for medicine.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Copper still yard: Coils and barrels create shiny clutter. Stream intake: Water feeds the operation quietly. Hidden storage lean-to: Crates and false walls hold secrets.

Plants and materials: sugar moss, smoke-stained bark, stream herbs. Animals and background life: drunk beetles, sugar moths, bold mice near mash barrels. The air carries sweet sour smell, copper shine, bubbling, soft smoke. Water feeds mash, mash feeds stills, waste feeds insects, and insects draw birds that give away the hiding place.

What people can get here: illicit drink, forest gossip, hidden route knowledge.
player_safe.known_for: The first sign is the smell: sugar smoke, wet bark, and something sharp enough to clean a wound. Then the trail frays into bootprints, bottle caps, and fern stems bent by people who know better than to leave a road. A copper coil glints between stacked firewood. Someone laughs too loudly from behind a canvas wall, then stops just long enough to count your shadows.
player_safe.culture_food: The cup you walked in with gets filled before you ask, clear liquor that smells like pears and lamp oil. A plate lands beside it without a word, smoked fish and a knob of sugar-moss candy and bread still warm from a lid that was part of a still an hour ago. Nobody names a price. Somebody waits to see whether you drink before they do.
player_safe.travel_texture: By the time the yard opens around you, a jug has already vanished under a chair and three people have decided whether to smile. The hand-painted labels all say medicinal use only. One old woman pours anyway, watching your hands instead of your face.

player_safe.name: Bramble Union Villages
player_safe.short: Vibrant, painted, moss-lit Bramble Union communities camouflaged behind mudstone walls and thorn protection.
player_safe.one_line: Vibrant, painted, moss-lit Bramble Union communities camouflaged behind mudstone walls and thorn protection.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Bramble Union villages are vibrant behind protection: painted mudstone, thorn screens, moss lamps, and people tired of being scenery in someone else's route.
player_safe.long_body:
These are living communities under pressure, not bandit camps. Gardens, repair-fires, children's paths, watch points, hunger, pride, and a great deal of defensive improvisation.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Screened entry path: Bramble walls hide where the village begins. Shared hearth: Food, tools, and argument gather at the center. Scrap ward yard: Stolen or salvaged charms are sorted and repurposed. Lookout trees: Watchers can see the road before the road sees them.

Plants and materials: bramble screens, root gardens, edible weeds, thorn vines trained into fences. Animals and background life: lean chickens, forest mice, watch birds trained with scraps. The air carries smoke kept low, whispered warnings, hidden footpaths, ward-scrap glints. The villages survive by hiding, sharing, repairing, and knowing the roads better than officials do.

What people can get here: improvised repairs, forest route knowledge, salvaged goods.
player_safe.known_for: Behind walls of trained thorn and painted mudstone, a whole village hides in plain sight. Gardens and repair-fires and children's paths fill the space within. Salvaged ward-charms get sorted and re-strung in a scrap yard. Watchers in the lookout trees see the road long before the road sees them, and everyone here is tired of being scenery in someone else's route.
player_safe.culture_food: Food is shared and stretched, root gardens, edible weeds, lean chickens, a stew that has plainly been added to for days. A guest gets a full bowl even when the bowl is thin, because pride here is fed before bellies are.
player_safe.travel_texture: The bramble screens part to reveal what the road could never see, color, paint, moss-lamps, low laughter kept deliberately quiet. Smoke is held close to the ground. Footpaths fork and double back, and you realize the whole village is built to be un-found.

player_safe.name: The Wandering Briar
player_safe.short: A mile-long living briar wall that blocks routes, shelters Wanderer families, and moves faster when its thorns taste blood.
player_safe.one_line: A mile-long living briar wall that blocks routes, shelters Wanderer families, and moves faster when its thorns taste blood.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Wandering Briar is a living wall with memory in its thorns, sheltering some people and punishing anyone who treats it like brush.
player_safe.long_body:
The Wandering Briar is a place that has learned to move: thorn walls, dragged doors, laundry, hidden hollows, and paths that are different the next time you look.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Thorn mouth: The entry looks like a plant trying to be a doorway. Dragged-room hollow: Old cart panels and doors create private pockets. Root skid trail: The ground shows where the place moved.

Plants and materials: living bramble, parasitic moss, latch-vines, thorn flowers that open after conflict. Animals and background life: mice in wall hollows, small birds using thorns as protection, insects that clean sap wounds. The air carries creaking thorn movement, sap smell, paths closing behind people, shadows full of gaps. The Briar shelters, snags, relocates, and regrows; damage changes its floor plan.

What people can get here: shelter if accepted, hidden routes, salvage.
player_safe.known_for: A living wall of thorn a mile long, and it moves. The way in looks like a plant trying to be a doorway. Old cart-panels and dragged doors make private rooms in the hollows. The ground shows long skid-marks where the whole thing relocated itself, and the path you came in by is not always the path that lets you out.
player_safe.culture_food: The Wanderer families share what the Briar provides, thorn-fruit that opens only after a fight, bitter greens, snared game. A welcomed guest eats from the same pot as everyone else. An unwelcome one finds the thorns suddenly much closer.
player_safe.travel_texture: Thorns creak and shift around you, and the sap smells green and sharp. Paths close quietly behind your back. Shadows are full of gaps that were not there a moment ago, and you understand the wall is deciding, slowly, whether to keep you.

player_safe.short_description: The Sable Sinecure™ makes moving freight through a deadly forest look so polished you forget the danger is the product.
player_safe.long_description: The Sable Sinecure™ presents as old-money competence: lacquered route maps, a hazard-rate ledger displayed like a wine list, agents in sable-and-silver who quote your survival odds with a sommelier's confidence. Buy a Certified Safe Passage™, a Hazard-Indexed™ premium route, a membership tier that makes paying more for the same trees feel like taste. It is a Kazrak™ franchise wearing heritage like cologne. player_safe.long_body:
Ember Lake is a quiet contradiction: water glowing like banked coals, warm shallows, black stones, steam curls, and boats that look too small for the light beneath them.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Warm shallows: The lake glows under clear water. Black-stone shore: Dark rocks hold heat after sunset. Boat landing: Small boats and heat charms mark practical use.

Plants and materials: steam reeds, ember algae, black-shore moss. Animals and background life: warm-water fish, ember flies, shore lizards, night birds hunting over steam. The air carries heat shimmer over water, coal-red glow, steam curls, warm stones. Warm vents feed algae, algae feed fish, fish draw birds, and locals read lake heat like weather.

What people can get here: boat crossing, warm fish, heated stones, lake-route lore.
player_safe.known_for: The cold gets to your fingers before the lake appears. Then the trees thin, and orange light moves under the black water like coals being stirred beneath glass. Steam beads on cloaks and eyelashes. Someone has left a kettle on a flat stone with no fire under it, and it is already starting to sing.
player_safe.culture_food: Dinner happens on the rocks. Someone lays a fish straight onto a stone too hot to touch and it hisses and curls and smells like the sea got lost in a forest. Kettles sit along the bank with nothing burning under them, steam climbing into the cold. The water you cup to your mouth tastes of warm iron, and everyone tells you it is good for your knees.
player_safe.travel_texture: People speak softer near the shore without agreeing to. Fish flash copper-bright below the surface. Barefoot bathers sit on volcanic rock while snowmelt drips from the branches above them. Every few minutes, the lake gives a low, warm pulse against the stones, like something sleeping far below has turned over.

block2.long_body:
Ember Lake is a quiet contradiction: water glowing like banked coals, warm shallows, black stones, steam curls, and boats that look too small for the light beneath them.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Warm shallows: The lake glows under clear water. Black-stone shore: Dark rocks hold heat after sunset. Boat landing: Small boats and heat charms mark practical use.

Plants and materials: steam reeds, ember algae, black-shore moss. Animals and background life: warm-water fish, ember flies, shore lizards, night birds hunting over steam. The air carries heat shimmer over water, coal-red glow, steam curls, warm stones. Warm vents feed algae, algae feed fish, fish draw birds, and locals read lake heat like weather.

What people can get here: boat crossing, warm fish, heated stones, lake-route lore.

The Glimpse.personality: Mercy older than fear, half-seen at the edge of the lantern light. It tends the hurt animals no one else will and asks for nothing, which is exactly why it unnerves people. To meet its many gentle eyes is to feel briefly, unbearably forgiven.
The Glimpse.wants: To shelter the wounded and the lost, and to be witnessed without being captured or named into a thing.
The Glimpse.fears: Iron cages, the hunter's certainty, and being turned from a kindness into a commodity.
The Glimpse.secrets: No forced reveal. Let this entity disclose truth through scene context and player attention.

player_safe.name: The Faceless Six
player_safe.public_face: The village leaders whose arrival turns hospitality into preparation, debate, and local accountability.
player_safe.short_description: The Faceless Six turn a friendly room into a village decision without raising their voices.
player_safe.long_description: The Faceless Six do not need thrones. They arrive as chairs being pulled closer, bowls set aside, and neighbors suddenly listening harder. Their authority is not spectacle. It is the weight of people who will still live here after the party leaves.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The room changes by inches. A chair scrapes. Someone closes the door against the damp. Six local figures settle into the kind of silence that asks whether guests understand consequence.

block1.name: The Faceless Six
block1.public_face: The village leaders whose arrival turns hospitality into preparation, debate, and local accountability.
block1.what_they_really_do: Holds Hush social memory and decides how much risk the village can absorb for outsiders.
block1.place_in_story: Act 3 social pressure and preparation beat; they make Hush feel governed rather than decorative.
block1.disposition_to_pcs: Watchful, practical, and responsive to respect for Hush.
block1.the_lever: Protect the village's agency; they cooperate when the party asks with humility instead of assuming command.

block2.standing: Local leadership body, strong inside Hush and limited beyond it.
block2.what_they_control: Local consensus, guest privileges, and who gets trusted with vulnerable information.
block2.how_they_operate: Argument, custom, quiet glances, and the old rhythm of people who have survived together.
block2.internal_tensions: Protective caution versus the need to help before the system tightens further.
block2.current_moves: Preparing Hush for possible ward strain without turning the village into panic.
block2.history_hook: A leadership custom from when Hush survived by making no single face responsible for every hard choice.

block3.who_they_prey_on: No one; they carry burden rather than extraction.

block4.aesthetic: Plain masks or veils in local custom, warm lamps, shared bowls, and a room that quiets when they enter.
voice: Measured village authority: We can welcome you and still ask what trouble followed you in.
block4.logo_hook: Six simple door marks around a clover.
block4.theme_song_hook: Seed only: six-part call-and-response under a hearth drone.

block5.relevance_to_players: Gives the table social permission, questions, and the sense that Hush is not a prop.
block5.relevance_to_world: Shows ordinary governance resisting corporate simplification.
block5.secrets: They know which neighbors quietly help Bramblefolk, but not every member agrees on what to risk.
block5.hidden_ties: GM-only: do not turn them into an exposition machine.

Young Dryads.personality: Children of the wood with bark for skin, shy until a kindness is broken. They guard the stones like a held breath, and they only turn fierce when a guest takes the welcome they were given and spits on it.
Young Dryads.wants: To tend their grove in peace and to see the old laws of hospitality kept by everyone who passes through.
Young Dryads.fears: Axes and fire, the Hunting Trees that were once kin gone wrong, and guests who smile and then steal.
Young Dryads.secrets: No forced reveal. Let this entity disclose truth through scene context and player attention.
body_language: Cluster around the stones, leaf-hair trembling, half-rooted and ready to flee.
Go very still and very green-eyed the moment a guest betrays the welcome.
sample_dialogue: A rustle that moves against the wind whenever you lie.
A creak of young wood, like a child deciding whether to trust you.

Dungeon Workers' Alliance.role: Sablewood labor lineage and pressure group behind Bramble-adjacent organizing
Dungeon Workers' Alliance.summary: The Dungeon Workers' Alliance is an old labor name that survives in brass pins, hand-copied maps, and tired defiance.
Dungeon Workers' Alliance.personality: Practical, tired, protective, and suspicious of corporate paperwork that arrives before help does.
Dungeon Workers' Alliance.wants: Preserve workers remembered as people with claims, graves, and skills instead of as route hazards.
Dungeon Workers' Alliance.fears: Being collapsed into Bramble violence, erased from records, or used as proof that all labor resistance is criminal.
Dungeon Workers' Alliance.secrets: Some Bramble Union routes and signals descend from old Alliance safety networks, but no one says this in front of a company clerk.
body_language: Pins are worn inside collars, not openly.
Old workers touch route ledgers like they are family records.
sample_dialogue: We built the road before they taught it to charge us rent.
Dungeon Workers' Alliance.search_or_loot: Evidence, not treasure: a strike notice, a route pin, or a list of missing workers can humanize the Bramble Union later.
Dungeon Workers' Alliance.gm_use: Use as earned depth if players ask why the Bramble Union has labor discipline, maps, or old security gear.
future_hooks: A future Relay Spire investigation can reveal Alliance records that contradict official hazard histories.

robust.gm_truth: GM-only: this is context, not a new exposition faction for the one-shot.
robust.appearance: Dull brass route pins, water-stained ledgers, faded strike notices, and hand-copied maps with names written beside unsafe bends.
robust.wants_pressures: Wants workers and freeholders remembered as people displaced by concessions, not converted into monster-road statistics.
robust.fears_vulnerabilities: Fears official files turning every dead worker into a hazard justification and every survivor into a criminal.
robust.story_use: Thematic kin to the Bramble Union and a future organized-resistance seed.

player_safe.name: Dungeon Workers' Alliance
player_safe.public_face: A half-legend of organized labor, old route pins, and workers who remember the dungeon never cleared itself.
player_safe.short_description: The Dungeon Workers' Alliance is an old labor name that survives in brass pins, hand-copied maps, and tired defiance.
player_safe.long_description: The Alliance feels less like a banner and more like a promise passed hand to hand. A dull brass pin in a collar, a copied route map with names by the dangerous bends, a worker who says 'we' when the company file says 'incident.'

block1.name: Dungeon Workers' Alliance
block1.public_face: A half-legend of organized labor, old route pins, and workers who remember the dungeon never cleared itself.
block1.what_they_really_do: Keeps names, claims, route memory, and solidarity alive after corporations convert workers into hazards.
block1.place_in_story: Thematic kin to the Bramble Union and a future organized-resistance seed.
block1.disposition_to_pcs: Cautious, practical, and moved by visible respect for workers.
block1.the_lever: Protect workers as people, not evidence, and Alliance-linked locals become safer to speak.

block2.standing: Buried but feared; the organized version of what the Bramble Union is reaching toward.
block2.what_they_control: Old route ledgers, mutual aid marks, worker names, and stories that corporate files tried to rename.
block2.how_they_operate: Pins inside collars, copied maps, remembered graves, and favors passed through people who still trust each other.
block2.internal_tensions: Some want open resistance; others know visibility gets workers killed or reclassified.
block2.current_moves: Survives as a rumor in Bramble route discipline and old worker marks.
block2.history_hook: A labor network born when dungeon danger became corporate product and workers started comparing notes.

block3.who_they_prey_on: No one; it organizes people preyed on by the danger economy.

block4.aesthetic: Dull brass pins, water-stained ledgers, strike notices, and hand-copied maps with names by unsafe bends.
voice: Worn, defiant, solidarity-plain: We built the road before they taught it to charge rent.
block4.logo_hook: Crossed pick and lantern under a shared hand.
block4.theme_song_hook: Seed only: work rhythm, low voices, no soloist.

block5.relevance_to_players: Can turn Bramble evidence from bandit proof into worker history.
block5.relevance_to_world: The Board fears organized labor more than desperate ambush.
block5.secrets: Some Bramble route signs descend from Alliance safety networks.
block5.hidden_ties: GM-only: this is context, not a new exposition faction for the one-shot.

player_safe.name: Dungeon Workers' Alliance
player_safe.public_face: A half-legend of organized labor, old route pins, and workers who remember the dungeon never cleared itself.
player_safe.short_description: The Dungeon Workers' Alliance is an old labor name that survives in brass pins, hand-copied maps, and tired defiance.
player_safe.long_description: The Alliance feels less like a banner and more like a promise passed hand to hand. A dull brass pin in a collar, a copied route map with names by the dangerous bends, a worker who says 'we' when the company file says 'incident.'
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The pin is small enough to hide under a collar. It shows a pick, a lantern, and a hand. It has been polished by fingers more often than cloth.

player_safe.name: The Midnight Cabal

player_safe.short_description: The Midnight Cabal is a rumor with a lockpick smile, present only in whispers and impossible coincidences.

outcomes.hard_failure: A flat read of The Tired Smile hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: The Tired Smile.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

rolls.hope_spin: Gain Hope. Let the Hope result make the scene more generous, clear, or player-directed when it fits the fiction.
rolls.fear_spin: GM gains Fear. Add pressure, reveal cost, spotlight a threat, or advance a visible consequence.

result_scale.botch: Roll 8 or less: give the red herring first - The first read treats the cheerful warning as ordinary safety copy, not evidence. Then add a visible cost such as lost time, a startled witness, a damaged trace, or corporate attention turning their way.
result_scale.miss: Roll below 13: give the Whisper only - Run the welcome broadcast sincerely, as if everyone agrees this is normal. The PC knows something is off, but the conclusion is not ready yet.
result_scale.hit: Roll 13 to 17: give the Nudge - Let one phrase land a little too cheerful: Certified Adventure Experience™ should sound proud of itself. If the roll lands with Fear, attach pressure: noise, delay, a suspicious look, or a clue that must be confirmed another way.
result_scale.clean: Roll 18 to 22: give the Spell-It-Out result - When contradicted later, say: remember the broadcast? It told you nature was the danger. The PC can say the useful conclusion out loud at the table.
result_scale.soar: Roll 23 or higher: give the Just-Tell-Them result - The broadcast was the official story, and the story keeps being wrong. Also point to one sibling clue or one nearby person/location that can confirm it.
result_scale.crit: On a critical success, use the Soar result, then let the PC ask one clean follow-up question about who, why, or what changed here. They gain Hope and clear 1 Stress if that is on the table.
